keyFindings.description: The four `… malformed` rows of TestDispatchPartialTailnetGroupNamesEveryMissingInput never assert that the bad value's own refusal fired; they rely on `valid` matching the resolver's check order. The signInDomain row has valid=0, so signInClientId's 'required' refusal fires first: with signInClause removed from the signInDomain refusal (dispatch.go:823) the subtest still passes (reviewer's mutation, reverted). The code-quality audit's scratch mutation (clause removed from the tailnetDnsName, tags and image refusals, tailnetAuthKey check moved first) left all four rows green. Fix: each row asserts the bad value's own refusal text (for example `signInDomain "Example.com" must be a lowercase DNS name`) plus the unset list, with an explicit per-row setup rather than a positional prefix.

Each group's checks are spread across newDispatchSettings: the tailnet group gated at :757, inside the shared image loop by frontDoorOnly and a clause column (:774-789), at :799 and again at :826; the sign-in group at :818 and :840, with region, natsUrl and natsSeedSecret between. Follow newDispatchAzure's pattern: one refuse function per mode (tailnet, sandbox, sign-in), each called once; the image loop goes back to the two app images. The comments at :135-140 (DispatchArgs: 'refuses each one missing, in the wording it always used') and :770-773 ('the sandbox block below' never checks the images) are false and go with it.

dispatchClusterOnlyRefusal's doc says a row sets an input 'alone on a valid cluster-only DispatchArgs'; its rows now also feed the two group tables and the Construct test. Rename it (the production type became dispatchInput for the same reason) and fix the doc.
